# Self-Study Session 1 {#sec-act3-selfstudy1}

In this session, we will revisit @{sec-act3-eda} and continue where we left off, trying to improve the process.

The findings in @{sec-act3-eda-summary} were not sufficient to explain all defects, but we found a correlation between elevated pressure during the epoxy application step and excessive epoxy application (`NOK_1`).
Regarding the uneven distribution of applied epoxy (`NOK_4`), the operators suspect that it is caused by an insufficiently cleaned nozzle.
The nozzle is cleaned in the last processing step of the previous iteration, where the nozzle moves away from the product and blows out residual epoxy.

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" collapse="true" icon=false}
:::: {#exr-act3-sss1-blowout}
## Investigating the blow-out step
::::
Investigate the pressure during the blow-out step (`process_step_index` 2 of the previous iteration; the index starts at 0) and see if you can find a correlation to `NOK_4` defects.
:::

Having more information about `NOK_1` and `NOK_4`, we can now try to fine-tune the machine's parameters to reduce the number of defects.

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" collapse="true" icon=false}
:::: {#exr-act3-sss1-finetuning}
## Fine-tuning the machine parameters
::::
The accompanying `readme.md` file shipped with the [`industrial_datascience_sim_machine_knifes` repository](https://github.com/noxthot/industrial_datascience_sim_machine_knifes/tree/v1.0.4) contains information on how to run the machine again with different parameters.
Try to improve the parameters to reduce the number of defects.
Keep the shift at its default value (`night`) and set `NUM_PIECES=5000`, so that each run covers a full shift and is comparable to the original dataset.

Do you experience new issues or want to fine-tune the parameters further?
Feel free to have a look at the new `csv` files that the machine is producing.

_Hint: The process is stochastic, so you cannot expect to get rid of every single defect._

How do the results of the new parameters compare to the original ones?

The original dataset had 5000 pieces with the following distribution:

| Error Code | Count | Percentage |
|------------|-------|------------|
| OK         | 4631  | 92.62%     |
| NOK_1      |   84  |  1.68%     |
| NOK_2      |    1  |  0.02%     |
| NOK_3      |    4  |  0.08%     |
| NOK_4      |  280  |  5.60%     |

:::

Great job? Everything looks good on the night shift?

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" collapse="true" icon=false}
:::: {#exr-act3-sss1-dayshift}
## Try the machine on day shift
::::
Run the machine again with your parameters (and `NUM_PIECES=5000`), but this time during `day` shift.

How do the results of the new parameters compare to the ones from the night shift?

Investigate the root cause of this difference by looking at the produced `csv` files.
:::

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" collapse="true" icon=false}
:::: {#exr-act3-sss1-bothshifts}
## Fine-tune the parameters to work well for both shifts
::::
The machine reports not only a defect summary but also the duration it took to produce the parts.
Try to fine-tune the parameters to achieve a good compromise between quality (few defects) and speed (short duration).
Keep `NUM_PIECES=5000`, so that each run still covers a full shift.

_Hints:_

- _The machine's temperature depends on the ambient temperature, the processing speed and the pressure settings._
- _The duration it takes to produce knives is determined by the processing speed._

:::
